clue.text: So-called disgraced person makes comeback as author

indicators.note: coming back means the disgraced person's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a disgraced person is one whose name is mud, so he is 'called' mud
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notorious figure stages a return as a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' points to the idiom 'his name is mud'. 'makes comeback' turns MUD into DUM, then AS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was the French novelist who wrote The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Cut short barrister's work

parts.note: to dock is to cut, as with a tail or wages
brief means short

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim a lawyer's job.
explanation.walkthrough: A dock brief was a case taken by a barrister directly from a prisoner in the dock, for a small fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A dock brief was a legal case handed to any available counsel by a defendant in court.

clue.text: Mount a single framed painting

indicators.note: framed means the first piece surrounds the second, like a picture frame

parts.note: MT is the usual abbreviation for Mount, as in Mt Everest
a single means one

explanation.surface: Hang up one picture in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb about hanging pictures, but it is the abbreviation MT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Monet is a canvas by the Impressionist Claude Monet, an artist's name standing for his work.

clue.text: Front of vessel near Cowes keeping off the rocks

indicators.note: keeping means the strait's name holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: the Solent is the strait beside Cowes on the Isle of Wight

indicators.note: front of means only the first letter of vessel is used

explanation.surface: A ship's bow off the Isle of Wight steers clear of the reef.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast; 'off the rocks' looks nautical but means out of financial trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that is off the rocks is no longer broke, able to pay its debts.

clue.text: Diabolical darkness, as a rule

parts.note: the Devil is called the Prince of Darkness, so his realm or rule is the domain of that title

explanation.surface: Evil gloom is usually the way of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like 'usually', but it means 'as a form of rule': the rank or territory of a prince, here the Prince of Darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: A princedom is the rank or realm governed by a prince, and the Devil is styled Prince of Darkness.

clue.text: Irishman in a film — shining appearance

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock crossword Irishman
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irish actor appears in a movie looking radiant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is not a movie but a thin surface layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin layer or sheen that forms on old bronze, wood or leather with age.

clue.text: Rigid rule for press cards one gets

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
the cards a player is dealt form a hand

explanation.surface: A strict regime for printing the cards a player receives.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron hand is harsh, inflexible control over others.

clue.text: Nephew on stage pronounced such a fool

indicators.note: pronounced means the stage name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Charley is the nephew in the farce Charley's Aunt

explanation.surface: A theatrical nephew is declared a complete idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Charley's Aunt is a Victorian stage farce whose hero Charley has his friend pose as his aunt; in British slang a 'charlie' is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, calling someone a right charlie means they are a silly idiot.

clue.text: Pupils punishment in Eton -it involved being in study

indicators.note: being in means the jumbled letters sit inside the word for a study

parts.note: a den is a private study or work room

indicators.note: involved means the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy penalty at Eton means being kept indoors at study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges ETON and IT into TENTIO, which 'being in' places inside DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Detention is the school sanction of keeping children back after classes.

clue.text: Sir Thomas's customs

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia; with the apostrophe it is his possessive
the accepted traditions and conventions of a society

explanation.surface: The habits belonging to a knight called Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are a community's norms of behaviour, and the possessive of More, Henry VIII's chancellor, sounds and spells the same.

clue.text: Artist allowed to scene of miracle first

indicators.note: first means the miracle's location goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: Cana in Galilee is where Jesus turned water into wine
let means allowed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter is permitted to visit a holy site before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Cana is the village of the wedding feast in John's gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the 18th-century Venetian painter famed for his views of Venice.

clue.text: The bloomer's a catastrophe if it's Diana's

definitions.text: The bloomer's a catastrophe if it's Diana's

parts.words: The bloomer's a catastrophe if it's Diana's
parts.note: a bloomer is a flower; put DI'S (Diana's) in front of this flower's name and you get a word for catastrophe

explanation.surface: A blunder becomes a disaster when a woman called Diana makes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a gaffe, but it is something that blooms, a flower; DI is the short form of Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michaelmas daisy is one kind of these star-shaped garden flowers.

clue.text: No man's land, where message is not explicit

definitions.meaning: the space separating two front lines or ruled rows
a meaning that is implied rather than stated outright

explanation.surface: The strip between trenches is where meaning goes unsaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspoken meaning is read in the gaps of a text, and no man's land is literally the strip separating two lines.

clue.text: How board meeting may end for occupant

definitions.meaning: a chess game on the board can finish with the winner announcing mate
someone who lives in a place, such as a prisoner or patient

explanation.surface: The way a directors' meeting might close, for a resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' suggests company directors, but it is a chess game, which ends 'in mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a resident of an institution such as a prison or hospital.

clue.text: Oh, to be in England" — for this parade?

definitions.text: Oh, to be in England" — for this parade?

parts.words: Oh, to be in England" — for this parade?
parts.note: Browning's poem continues 'Now that April's there', so the month before has gone by; also a troop parade in step

explanation.surface: A homesick quotation offered as a reason for a military procession.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning's Home-Thoughts, from Abroad begins 'Oh, to be in England now that April's there': the previous month is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial parade of troops filing past a saluting dignitary is named for the marching, with the month also gone.

clue.text: Domestic removed from seaside position

definitions.meaning: home affairs, as opposed to foreign ones

explanation.surface: A servant is taken away from a job by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' reads as a servant, but it means home affairs, as in a ministry of the interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Home affairs are handled by an interior ministry, and the inland part of a country is far from its coast.

clue.text: One has no common ground with this element

parts.note: something not common is rare
earth means ground or soil

explanation.surface: Someone with no shared footing is linked to this substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has ... with this' is padding to make the sentence: the solver takes 'no common' and 'ground' as the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanides such as cerium and neodymium are a family of metallic elements known by this name.

clue.text: Punctual about bride's gift

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
a dot is a dowry, from French, so the bride's gift is the dot

explanation.surface: Arriving on time with a present for the bride.
explanation.walkthrough: DOT, a dowry brought by a bride, is an old borrowing from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arriving at exactly the right time is punctual, at the precise moment.

clue.text: Coin far better out of Sydney Carton's final act

indicators.note: out of means the following words are removed from the quoted phrase

parts.note: Carton's last words in A Tale of Two Cities: 'It is a far, far better thing that I do'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coin is much the better for being part of a fictional hero's last deed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities, Carton goes to the guillotine in another's place calling it 'a far, far better thing'; strike 'far better' from that. A farthing was a quarter of an old British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was a small pre-decimal British coin worth a quarter of a penny.

clue.text: He'd admit nothing in forming American party

indicators.note: in means the zero is put inside the letters of He'd

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, means nothing
to own up is to admit

explanation.surface: A man would confess to nothing while organising a US celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively country-dance gathering in rural America.

clue.text: Batsman who received quite a good hand?

definitions.meaning: a cricketer who goes in first to bat

definitions.text: who received quite a good hand?
definitions.meaning: in card games such as poker, a player needs strong cards to start the betting

explanation.surface: A cricketer who was given decent applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good hand' suggests applause for a batsman, but in poker a minimum hand is needed to start the betting.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening batsman starts a cricket innings, and in cards the first bidder needs strong cards.

clue.text: Attack abandoned -beat it thus

parts.note: a push is a military attack or offensive
off means called off, abandoned

explanation.surface: An offensive is cancelled, so clear off in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it' looks like a fight word, but it is slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang imperatives telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Bridge club

definitions.meaning: a cue rest used in billiards or snooker

explanation.surface: A card-game society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge club' reads as one card society, but each word is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a cue rest has this name, and so did an old golf iron with a narrow face.

clue.text: Getting measure of heats, reaches the final, perhaps

definitions.text: Getting measure of heats, reaches the final, perhaps

parts.words: Getting measure of heats, reaches the final, perhaps
parts.note: read as sport, a runner getting through the heats reaches the final; read as physics, it is a system for measuring how hot things are

explanation.surface: An athlete sizing up the heats makes it to the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heats' and 'final' suggest a race, but the clue is about temperatures, measured on a scale with 212 degrees for boiling water.
explanation.definitionFit: The temperature scale with water freezing at 32 degrees is named after the physicist who devised it.

clue.text: Nameless ally got overheated

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation N for name is taken away

parts.note: a friend is an ally

explanation.surface: An anonymous partner became too hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked in hot fat is this, and overheated people are said to be this.

clue.text: Distribute a levy raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word for levy is read upwards

parts.note: a toll is a levy or charge

explanation.surface: Hand out the proceeds of a tax that has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or assign portions.

clue.text: From Florida, hoped to see another state

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A Floridian hopes to visit a different US state.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-western US state is famous for potatoes, so it is another state as well as Florida.

clue.text: Follow and arrest boxer's band

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Tail and catch a fighter's gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is a dog breed, and 'band' is its neck strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckband worn by a pet such as a boxer is a strap around its throat.

clue.text: Return list perceived as part of mine

indicators.note: return means the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
noted means perceived

explanation.surface: Send back a list of what one saw in a coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reverses ROTA and NOTED together, ROTANOTED read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive mine is set off by a firing device inside it.

clue.text: Realize it's a trick

definitions.meaning: to sell for, as in an item realizing a price

explanation.surface: Understand that it is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realize' means bring in a sum at sale, not understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting may bring in a good price at auction, and an old sense of the word is a dodge or ruse.
